title: TrackFlow Telemetry Event Schemas
description: Standard Event Envelope (EE) and per-event property allowlists for the TrackFlow backoffice (inventory + centralized incident manager) and API. Human-readable companion: telemetry-plan.md.

event_id.description: Unique event id (UUIDv4). Idempotency key at the collector.

timestamp.description: Emission time in ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-10-05T20:34:00.000Z.

session_id.description: Browsing/session id. Backend derives it from the request when the client does not provide one.

user_id.description: TinyDB user id. null for anonymous or pre-authentication events.

event_type.description: Closed enum of event types. Must match a key in the events catalog.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the properties schema for this event_type. Starts at 1.0.0.

request_id.description: Correlation id for the originating request/flow. Ties frontend and backend events together.

properties.description: Event-specific payload. Must satisfy the allowlist of the matching event_type.

warehouse.description: Warehouse. Country is derived: los_angeles -> USA, zaragoza -> Spain.

client_id.description: B2B client (brand) that owns the SKU. PREREQUISITE: field not yet present in the SKU ORM.

product_category.description: PREREQUISITE: field not yet present in the SKU ORM.

path.description: Normalized route path without query string or identifiers, e.g. /inventory.

incident_category.description: Incident category. Source of truth: services/api/models.py INCIDENT_CATEGORIES.

incident_status.description: Incident status. Source of truth: services/api/models.py INCIDENT_STATUSES.

incident_branch.description: Incident branch/site. Source of truth: services/api/models.py INCIDENT_BRANCHES.

incident_origin.description: Incident origin. Source of truth: services/api/models.py INCIDENT_ORIGINS.

inbound_order_created.description: A warehouse registers the receipt of merchandise from a client (stock entry).
inbound_order_created.processing_rationale: Feeds Ana's near-real-time warehouse volume and operations view; used for capacity and staffing planning.
inbound_order_created.golden_rule: We capture inbound_order_created because we need to know how much volume enters per client and warehouse, which lets us plan warehouse capacity and staffing (Ana).

outbound_order_created.description: A warehouse completes picking and dispatch of an order (stock exit).
outbound_order_created.processing_rationale: Bottleneck and SLA detection require low latency; feeds Ana's live operations view.
outbound_order_created.golden_rule: We capture outbound_order_created because we need to know how many orders are processed per client and warehouse and at what pace, which lets us detect operational bottlenecks before they hit delivery SLA (Ana).

stock_threshold_triggered.description: A SKU's stock falls below the minimum configured for that client.
stock_threshold_triggered.processing_rationale: Triggers an immediate alert to the client and the commercial team before a stockout; latency matters.
stock_threshold_triggered.golden_rule: We capture stock_threshold_triggered because we need to know how often a client runs out of a SKU, which lets us alert the client and the commercial team before a stockout (Miguel).

quantity.description: Current stock after the triggering movement.

min_stock.description: Configured minimum. PREREQUISITE: threshold config not yet present.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: A user attempts to modify stock directly (outside an order) and the system rejects it. Guard for the rule 'stock is never edited directly'.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.processing_rationale: Traceability/security tripwire; the team needs to react quickly where bypass attempts concentrate.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.golden_rule: We capture direct_stock_edit_rejected because we need to know whether warehouse staff try to bypass traceability controls, which lets us reinforce training or permissions in the warehouse where this happens most often.

inventory_discrepancy_detected.description: A physical count or audit detects a difference between system stock and real stock. Anchored to an incident with category inventory_discrepancy.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.processing_rationale: Drives weekly audit prioritization; no real-time operational action is taken per event.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.golden_rule: We capture inventory_discrepancy_detected because we need to know in which SKUs and warehouses discrepancies occur most, which lets us prioritize inventory audits on the SKUs with the highest discrepancy rate (Ana).

quantity.description: Counted quantity reported by the audit.

order_id.description: Outbound order affected by the discrepancy; one event per order.

session_started.processing_rationale: Usage/adoption analytics only; daily aggregation is sufficient.
session_started.golden_rule: We capture session_started because we need to know when and how often sessions begin, which lets us measure adoption of the backoffice.

login_succeeded.description: A user successfully authenticates via POST /api/auth/login.
login_succeeded.processing_rationale: Adoption baselines; aggregated daily, no per-event action.
login_succeeded.golden_rule: We capture login_succeeded because we need to know successful logins per role, which lets us track adoption and establish access baselines.

login_failed.description: A login attempt is rejected (e.g. HTTP 401). Never carries email or password.
login_failed.processing_rationale: Security: detect credential stuffing or brute-force patterns early.
login_failed.golden_rule: We capture login_failed because we need to know failed login attempts, which lets us detect credential stuffing and authentication UX friction.

session_expired.description: The session token is missing, invalid or expired (HTTP 401 on /auth/me or any protected request).
session_expired.processing_rationale: Used to tune token TTL and re-auth UX over time; not a per-event operational action.
session_expired.golden_rule: We capture session_expired because we need to know how often sessions die mid-task, which lets us tune token TTL and the re-authentication experience.

page_view.description: High-frequency frontend navigation event. One per effective route visit (debounced and deduplicated).
page_view.processing_rationale: High volume, product analytics; aggregated offline, no per-event action.
page_view.throttle: Debounce 500 ms per route; dedupe by (session_id, path) within a 1 s window. Emit once per effective navigation, not per render. Sampling 100% now; reduce to 10-20% under peak if ingest cost requires it.
page_view.golden_rule: We capture page_view because we need to know which pages are visited and how often, which lets us prioritize UX investment.

pages_visited_in_session.description: Aggregate of pages visited during a session. Emitted once per session on expiry, logout or inactivity timeout.
pages_visited_in_session.processing_rationale: Derived metric computed at session end; consumed by analytics only.
pages_visited_in_session.throttle: Emit once per session (on session_expired, explicit logout, or 30 min inactivity).
pages_visited_in_session.golden_rule: We capture pages_visited_in_session because we need to know navigation depth per session, which lets us tune engagement and information architecture.

order_form_opened.description: An operator opens the inbound/outbound order form for a SKU.
order_form_opened.processing_rationale: Funnel measurement; aggregated, no live alerting.
order_form_opened.golden_rule: We capture order_form_opened because we need to know how many order flows start, which lets us measure funnel conversion into registered orders.

order_form_abandoned.description: An order form is opened but not submitted (closed, navigated away or timed out).
order_form_abandoned.processing_rationale: UX friction analysis; aggregated, no per-event action.
order_form_abandoned.throttle: Debounce on visibilitychange/blur with a 30 s grace timer; cancel if the form is submitted or reopened. One event per abandoned flow, not per field.
order_form_abandoned.golden_rule: We capture order_form_abandoned because we need to know where operators abandon order creation, which lets us reduce friction in the order flow.

stock_validation_failed.description: Server-side validation of an order fails (quantity, warehouse or sku_id).
stock_validation_failed.processing_rationale: Repeated failures signal a systemic/broken form or integration; react quickly.
stock_validation_failed.golden_rule: We capture stock_validation_failed because we need to know which validation errors happen, which lets us improve form guidance and fix systemic issues.

outbound_rejected_insufficient_stock.description: An outbound order is rejected because requested quantity exceeds available stock in the target warehouse (HTTP 400, check-then-write, no write).
outbound_rejected_insufficient_stock.processing_rationale: Feeds inventory planning and client alerts with low latency.
outbound_rejected_insufficient_stock.golden_rule: We capture outbound_rejected_insufficient_stock because we need to know how often outbound fails for lack of stock, which lets us improve inventory planning and alert clients.

incident_form_opened.description: An operator opens the 'new incident' form from the incidents page (+ Nueva incidencia).
incident_form_opened.processing_rationale: Funnel measurement for the incident manager; aggregated, no live action.
incident_form_opened.golden_rule: We capture incident_form_opened because we need to know how many incident reports start, which lets us measure funnel conversion into created incidents.

incident_created.description: An incident is created through the centralized incident manager (POST /api/incidents, 201). Free-text description is never sent.
incident_created.processing_rationale: The incident inventory feeds operational triage (Ana) and the executive view; low latency is useful.
incident_created.golden_rule: We capture incident_created because we need to know incident volume by category, branch and origin, which lets us prioritize root-cause work and staffing where incidents concentrate (Ana).

description_length.description: Length of the free-text description. The text itself is never captured.

incident_validation_failed.description: Server-side validation of incident creation fails (missing/invalid field, HTTP 400).
incident_validation_failed.processing_rationale: Repeated failures signal a broken form or a missing domain value; react quickly.
incident_validation_failed.throttle: Deduplicate by (reason, field, branch) within 60 s so a single operator retrying does not create an alert storm.
incident_validation_failed.golden_rule: We capture incident_validation_failed because we need to know which incident fields fail validation, which lets us improve the incident form and fix systemic gaps.

incident_status_change_opened.description: An operator opens the status-flow modal for an incident (Cambiar estado).
incident_status_change_opened.processing_rationale: Usage/funnel measurement; aggregated, no live action.
incident_status_change_opened.golden_rule: We capture incident_status_change_opened because we need to know how often operators open the status flow, which lets us measure whether incidents actually move forward.

incident_status_changed.description: An incident status transition succeeds (PATCH /api/incidents/{id}/status, 200). Only emitted when the state actually changes.
incident_status_changed.processing_rationale: Resolution-time and backlog monitoring need low latency to feed the incident SLA view.
incident_status_changed.golden_rule: We capture incident_status_changed because we need to know how fast incidents move between states, which lets us reduce incident backlog and resolution time (Ana).

time_in_status_seconds.description: Seconds spent in from_status before the transition.

incident_transition_rejected.description: An incident status transition is rejected because it is not allowed or the incident is in a final state (HTTP 400).
incident_transition_rejected.processing_rationale: Permission/UX friction tripwire; the team needs to react quickly where rejections concentrate.
incident_transition_rejected.throttle: Deduplicate by (attempted_status, from_status, branch) within 60 s to avoid storms from repeated retries.
incident_transition_rejected.golden_rule: We capture incident_transition_rejected because we need to know which state transitions are rejected and why, which lets us detect UX or permission friction and misused flows.

api_response_time.description: High-frequency backend latency metric. Not emitted per request: aggregated into 60 s buckets keyed by (method, path, status_code).
api_response_time.processing_rationale: High volume; percentiles are computed in windows for performance dashboards and regression detection.
api_response_time.throttle: Aggregate in a 60 s window keyed by (method, path, status_code); flush one event per bucket with duration_ms = p50/p95 or request count. In-process buffer, flush on timer or size threshold.
api_response_time.golden_rule: We capture api_response_time because we need to know API latency per endpoint, which lets us detect performance regressions.

frontend_error_uncaught.description: An unhandled frontend error (window.onerror or unhandledrejection). Message is sanitized and truncated; no full stack is stored.
frontend_error_uncaught.processing_rationale: Stability alerting; users must not be the first to notice a broken build.
frontend_error_uncaught.throttle: Deduplicate identical errors by (error_name, error_message_sanitized, path) within 60 s to avoid error storms.
frontend_error_uncaught.golden_rule: We capture frontend_error_uncaught because we need to know unhandled JS errors and their routes, which lets us fix stability issues before users report them.
